avalancheActivity.comment:
Weak layers in the lower part of the snowpack can be released even by individual winter sport participants. This applies on steep west, north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m, as well as in all aspects above approximately 3000 m. Remotely triggered avalanches are possible in isolated cases. This applies in high Alpine regions. Mostly avalanches are medium-sized.
In addition the fresh wind slabs should be taken into account. Such avalanche prone locations are to be found in steep terrain above approximately 2400 m. Caution is to be exercised adjacent to ridgelines, as well as in gullies and bowls, and behind abrupt changes in the terrain. The number and size of avalanche prone locations will increase with altitude. Avalanches can reach medium size.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
avalancheActivity.highlights: Weak layers in the old snowpack necessitate caution. Fresh wind slabs require caution.

snowpackStructure.comment:
Avalanche prone weak layers exist in the old snowpack. This applies in particular on west, north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m, as well as in all aspects above approximately 3000 m. Whumpfing sounds and the formation of shooting cracks when stepping on the snowpack and fresh avalanches serve as an alarm indicating the danger.

In many areas 15 to 20 cm of snow fell on Thursday,, and locally up to 30 cm. The wind has transported the new snow. This applies in particular at high altitudes and in high Alpine regions. The fresh wind slabs are lying on soft layers.

tendency.highlights: The avalanche danger will persist. Experience in the assessment of avalanche danger is required.

avalancheActivity.comment:
Weak layers in the old snowpack can be released even by individual winter sport participants. This applies in particular on very steep west, north and east facing slopes between approximately 2400 and 2900 m. Caution is to be exercised in particular in gullies and bowls, and behind abrupt changes in the terrain. Avalanches are rather small.
In addition the fresh wind slabs should be taken into account. Such avalanche prone locations are to be found in steep terrain above approximately 2200 m and adjacent to ridgelines. They are mostly small. They are clearly recognisable to the trained eye.
Along the border with Vorarlberg individual gliding avalanches are possible, but they will be mostly small.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

snowpackStructure.comment:
Under the various new snow and snow-drift layers that formed in the middle of November you find between approximately 2400 and 2900 m in some places a weak layer consisting of facets. Whumpfing sounds and the formation of shooting cracks when stepping on the snowpack can indicate the danger.

In many areas 10 to 20 cm of snow fell on Thursday,, and locally even larger amounts. The wind has transported the new snow. This applies in particular at high altitudes and in high Alpine regions. The fresh wind slabs are lying on soft layers.
